The REST module's direct callers of `EncounterService.saveEncounter` are all in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`. Each one is a `save` or `delete` override on a generic delegating resource, so a behaviour change in `saveEncounter` would reach these `/ws/rest/v1` endpoints:

1. **`EncounterResource1_8.save`** (`openmrs1_8/EncounterResource1_8.java:189-191`): the base `/encounter` create/update path. It returns the service's result directly.
2. **`EncounterResource1_9.save`** (`openmrs1_9/EncounterResource1_9.java:77-86`): the 1.9 override. It sets the back-reference on `encounterProviders` first, then calls `saveEncounter` and returns the delegate.
3. **`EncounterProviderResource1_9.save`** (`openmrs1_9/EncounterProviderResource1_9.java:182-200`): adds a provider to the encounter, saves the whole encounter, then re-reads the persisted provider so its UUID is correct. It depends on the saved encounter's provider collection.
4. **`EncounterProviderResource1_9.delete`** (`openmrs1_9/EncounterProviderResource1_9.java:162-175`): voids the matching provider and saves the parent encounter.

Test code that calls `saveEncounter` in the same module would also show a behaviour change, so I've listed those last. I did not search the other modules (emrapi, fhir2, and so on) and did not inspect the `openmrs-core` callers beyond the grep results. The `openmrs-core` callers are inside core, not the REST module, so they are out of scope.
